root.label: Namespaces and scope
root.note: Where a declaration is visible, and how named, reopenable namespace scopes combine.

children.label: Kinds of scope
children.note: Namespace, class, enumeration, block, function parameter, lambda and template parameter.

children.label: Block scopes
children.note: Compound statements, each if, switch, loop and handler introduce one.

children.label: P1787R6
children.note: C++23 rewording: declarations inhabit and target scopes and bind names.

children.label: P2036R3
children.note: A lambda's trailing return type sees its init-captures; applied as a defect report.

children.label: Point of declaration
children.note: The locus where a name starts to be visible.

children.label: Variables
children.note: After the declarator, before the initializer: char n[n] uses the outer n.

children.label: Enumerators
children.note: After the initializer, so k = k + 5 reads the outer k.

children.label: Complete-class contexts
children.note: Member function bodies and default arguments see members declared later.

children.label: Block scope
children.note: Inner declarations hide outer ones of the same name.

children.label: Shadowing
children.note: Legal and silent; hidden globals are reachable with ::, hidden locals are not.

children.label: Forbidden redeclarations
children.note: Parameters in the outer body block, condition names in if or else bodies.

children.label: -Wshadow
children.note: GCC and Clang warn about shadowing only when asked.

children.label: Namespaces
children.note: Named scopes that can be reopened in any file.

children.label: Qualified definitions
children.note: Define a member outside only after declaring it, from an enclosing namespace.

children.label: Nested definitions
children.note: namespace a::b::c is C++17; namespace a::inline b is C++20.

children.label: Aliases
children.note: namespace fs = std::filesystem; an alias cannot reopen the namespace.

children.label: Unnamed namespaces
children.note: A unique name plus a using-directive; same-named globals become ambiguous.

children.label: Using-directives
children.note: using namespace N declares nothing; it only changes unqualified lookup.

children.label: Nearest enclosing rule
children.note: Names act as if declared in the nearest namespace enclosing directive and target.

children.label: Transitive
children.note: A directive for B also brings in namespaces that B nominates.

children.label: Ambiguity on use
children.note: Two directives bringing the same name only fail when it is used unqualified.

children.label: Inline namespaces
children.note: Members act as members of the enclosing namespace for most purposes.

children.label: ABI versioning
children.note: The inline name stays in mangled names, like std::__cxx11 and std::__1.

children.label: Specialization
children.note: Templates can be specialized through the enclosing namespace's name.

children.label: First definition
children.note: inline must appear on the first definition; adding it later is ill-formed.
